question: What will be the average daily mean temperature in Mexico City over the 7 days ending September 23, 2026, in degrees Celsius?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the mean of the daily mean 2-metre air temperatures from 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-23 at latitude 19.43, longitude -99.13 (Mexico City), from the ERA5 reanalysis as served by the Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com), in degrees Celsius.
research:
Here are the findings, using only information published on or before 2026-09-09. Since 2019, the Sept 17-23 average at this grid point has ranged from 16.26 to 17.66°C, and early September 2026 is running mid-range. All the averages below are my own calculations from the Open-Meteo daily values.

## 1. Resolution source
- Source: Open-Meteo ERA5 archive, daily `temperature_2m_mean`, at 19.43, -99.13. The API snaps this to the grid cell at about 19.44N, 99.11W. [Open-Meteo archive](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2026-08-01&end_date=2026-09-08&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2026-09-08: the latest value available is 16.9°C. Daily values for Sept 1-8 were 16.2, 17.1, 17.9, 18.5, 17.8, 16.5, 16.3 and 16.9, which average 17.15°C. [Open-Meteo archive](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2026-08-01&end_date=2026-09-08&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- August 2026: daily values ranged from 15.5 (Aug 24) to 20.4 (Aug 4), and the second half of the month mostly sat between 16 and 18°C. [Open-Meteo archive](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2026-08-01&end_date=2026-09-08&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The window (Sept 17-23) starts 8 days after the forecast deadline.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-09-08: the SMN-based forecast for CDMX on Sept 9 gave a high of 24-26°C, a low of 13-15°C, cloudy skies and afternoon showers. Tropical wave 37 was active and wave 38 was approaching Yucatán. The north of Mexico had heat waves. [Grupo Animal](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/clima-septiembre-lluvias-nublado-cdmx-edomex)
- 2026-09-07 and 09-08: forecasts called for light to strong rain and cloudy skies in CDMX, which is typical of the rainy season. [Grupo Animal 8 Sep](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/pronostico-del-clima-en-cdmx-martes-8-de-septiembre), [Grupo Animal 7 Sep](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/pronostico-del-clima-en-cdmx-lunes-7-de-septiembre)
- 2026-08-13: the CPC put out an El Niño Advisory. A repost of the discussion says El Niño is strengthening, with a "greater than 90% chance of a very strong event" in fall and winter 2026-27. I couldn't check that wording against the original text, so treat it with some caution. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_disc_aug2026/ensodisc.shtml), [Coyote Gulch](https://coyotegulch.blog/2026/08/14/the-august-13-2026-el-nino-southern-oscillation-enso-diagnostic-discussion-is-hot-off-the-presses-from-the-climate-prediction-center/)

## 4. Base rates
Sept 17-23 average of daily means, same grid point (Open-Meteo/ERA5):
- 2025: 17.37 (daily 16.1 to 18.6). [2025](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2025-09-01&end_date=2025-09-30&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2024: 17.66 (16.9 to 18.6). [2024](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2024-09-01&end_date=2024-09-30&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2023 (El Niño year): 17.54 (16.5 to 18.5). [2023](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2023-09-01&end_date=2023-09-30&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2022: 16.26 (16.0 to 16.5). [2022](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2022-09-01&end_date=2022-09-30&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2021: 16.57 (15.2 to 17.6). [2021](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2021-09-01&end_date=2021-09-30&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2020: 16.59. [2020](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2020-09-17&end_date=2020-09-23&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2019: 17.50. [2019](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2019-09-17&end_date=2019-09-23&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- 2015 (strong El Niño): 16.26. [2015](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=19.43&longitude=-99.13&start_date=2015-09-17&end_date=2015-09-23&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=auto)
- Across 2019-2025 the mean is about 17.07 and the standard deviation about 0.55. Results split into a cooler group (16.3 to 16.6) and a warmer group (17.4 to 17.7). The last three years were all warm.
- The two El Niño analogs disagree: 2023 was warm and 2015 was cool.

How the Sept 1-8 average compares with the Sept 17-23 average:
- 2021: 16.34, then 16.57 (+0.23)
- 2022: 16.81, then 16.26 (-0.55)
- 2023: 17.55, then 17.54 (0.0)
- 2024: 17.15, then 17.66 (+0.51)
- 2025: 16.73, then 17.37 (+0.64)
- 2026: 17.15, then unknown. This ties 2024 and sits mid-to-upper among recent years, above 2021, 2022 and 2025 and below 2023.
- In these five years the change from early September to the window ranged from -0.55 to +0.64, with no consistent seasonal drift.
- Single days in the window can swing by 1 to 2°C, mainly from cloud cover and rain. Cold fronts arriving in late September can drop daily means to around 14-15°C, as happened in late September of 2022 and 2024.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question, and no expert numeric forecast for this window.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- I couldn't find an official SMN outlook covering Sept 17-23 that was published by Sept 9. Only daily forecasts were available.
- The main things that could move the result:
  - Rain and cloud from tropical waves, and possibly tropical cyclones, would cool the days.
  - Any early cold front ("frente frío") would push the average down.
  - A drier pattern under El Niño would allow warmer afternoons.
- El Niño is strengthening (CPC, 2026-08-13). It is often linked with less rain over central Mexico late in the rainy season, though the 2015 and 2023 analogs pointed in opposite directions. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_disc_aug2026/ensodisc.shtml)
- The next CPC ENSO discussion is due 2026-10-08, after resolution. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml)
